answer: Double-Entry Action Ledger. Each agent identity broadcasts a signed action signal committed to a shared append-only ledger; any later identity repeating a prior entry must harbor the original's full history to execute. Duplicate lineages thus collide on the same ledger slots and self-expose. An attacker cloning N agents pays N distinct durable storage and sync costs, plus a falcon probe: a randomly assigned auditor identity traces each claimed lineage to its root within a fixed window, and untraceable roots are frozen.
